question: Flights from London to Los Angeles pass over Greenland, far north of a straight line on a flat map. Why?
options: It is the shortest route on a globe
To stay near airports for emergencies
answer: It is the shortest route on a globe. The shortest path between two points on a sphere is a great circle, and on a Mercator map great circles bow towards the pole. Stretch a string between London and Los Angeles on a globe and it runs over Greenland and northern Canada.
move: A straight line on a flat map is rarely the shortest path on Earth.
ask: Which route or plan looks direct only because of how it was drawn?
trap: Thinking the straight line on a flat map is the shortest.
source: Great Circle Mapper, London Heathrow to Los Angeles
